content.title: Crime Maps & Statistics
content.summary: The Arvada Police Department offers public access to local crime data through the LexisNexis Community Crime Map, which allows users to explore recent crime trends by searching for specific addresses and dates. Crime statistics are reported in accordance with the National Incident-Based Reporting System, but the data may be recategorized, and ongoing investigations could alter details. Yearly crime trends indicate fluctuations in various categories, with a total of 6,812 reported crimes in 2023, compared to 6,723 in 2022.
content.body:
## Community Crime Map

The Arvada Police Department provides public access to local crime data through the [LexisNexis Community Crime Map](https://communitycrimemap.com/), an online tool that supports transparency and awareness by allowing users to explore recent crime trends in their area.

### How it works

Most Arvada crime data is uploaded to the Map on a daily basis. Users can search by address, date range, time, and broad crime categories to see a snapshot of activity in the community.

### Important note about crime categories

The Arvada Police Department reports crime data in accordance with the National Incident-Based Reporting System (NIBRS), part of the FBI’s Uniform Crime Reporting (UCR) program. However, when this data is shared via the Community Crime Map, it is recategorized into general incident types based on the Map’s own classification system. As a result, the information shown may not fully align with how the incident was originally reported or classified by Arvada PD.

In addition, crime details may change during ongoing investigations, and the map should not be used as an official record of police activity. For verified or official statistics, contact the Arvada Police Records Unit at 720-898-6920, or visit the [Colorado Crime Statistics webpage](https://coloradocrimestats.state.co.us/tops).
